CausalChain: Metabolic dysregulation in NASH -> Increased hepatic iron storage in ferritin -> Activation of NCOA4-mediated ferritinophagy -> Release of labile iron into the cytosol -> Labile iron participates in Fenton reactions -> Enhanced lipid peroxidation via enzymes such as ACSL4 and LPCAT3 -> Accumulation of toxic lipid peroxides -> Induction of hepatocyte ferroptosis -> Progression to liver injury and fibrosis
Hypothesis: Selective inhibition of NCOA4-mediated ferritinophagy in hepatocytes will reduce labile iron release and subsequent lipid peroxidation, thereby decreasing ferroptosis and mitigating the progression of liver injury and fibrosis in NASH.
Abstract: Non-alcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH) and related chronic liver diseases are characterized by iron accumulation and excessive lipid peroxidation, both of which contribute to hepatocyte ferroptosis and subsequent liver damage. Building on emerging evidence that ferritinophagy releases labile iron and that lipid remodeling enzymes facilitate peroxidation, our hypothesis posits that the selective inhibition of NCOA4-mediated ferritinophagy in hepatocytes may reduce labile iron levels and curtail lipid peroxidation. This targeted intervention could prevent ferroptotic cell death and thus slow the progression of liver injury toward fibrosis.
